actions.text: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: (2/3 required): 381 - 31 (Roll no. 217). (text: 07/21/2025 CR H3508)
Passed/agreed to in House: On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: (2/3 required): 381 - 31 (Roll no. 217). (text: 07/21/2025 CR H3508)
Considered as unfinished business. (consideration: CR H3621-3622)

At the conclusion of debate, the Yeas and Nays were demanded and ordered. Pursuant to the provisions of clause 8, rule XX, the Chair announced that further proceedings on the motion would be postponed.
DEBATE - The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 3357.
Considered under suspension of the rules. (consideration: CR H3508)
Mr. Hill (AR) moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended.
Placed on the Union Calendar, Calendar No. 90.
Reported (Amended) by the Committee on Financial Services. H. Rept. 119-120.

dimensions.assessment: Affects publicly traded corporate issuers with multi-class share structures, their directors, executive officers, and large shareholders.
dimensions.evidence: each issuer with a multi-class share structure to disclose the information... with respect to each person who is a director, director nominee, or named executive officer

dimensions.assessment: Administrative disclosure requirement in corporate proxy materials rather than a structural change to corporate governance rules.
dimensions.evidence: disclose the information described in paragraph (2) in any proxy or consent solicitation material

dimensions.assessment: No direct federal spending or revenue implications stated in the text.
Amends Section 14 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 to direct the SEC to promulgate specific disclosure rules.
dimensions.evidence: Section 14 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (15 U.S.C. 78n) is amended

dimensions.assessment: Permanent regulatory disclosure requirement for annual shareholder meetings and proxy solicitations.
dimensions.evidence: in any proxy or consent solicitation material for an annual meeting of the shareholders of the issuer

missing_information: The exact number of registered public companies currently utilizing multi-class share structures.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill requires issuers with multi-class share structures to disclose specific voting power and share ownership percentages for directors, executives, and major beneficial owners in proxy materials.
